description: Hi! I'm a software developer from Peru, passionate about technology, music, and science. I enjoy exploring how different fields can come together to create new experiences. For this challenge, I want to turn data from our planet into sounds, music, and stories that anyone can explore. I'm looking for curious, creative people interested in Earth science, design, data visualization, or web development. What matters most is sharing ideas and building something together!
summary:
GEAVOX is an interactive, browser-based geospatial sonification explorer built for NASA’s "The Earth Information Jukebox" challenge. Using official global precipitation imagery from NASA’s Earth Information Center (EIC) Content Database and Scientific Visualization Studio (SVS 4285, GPM/IMERG), GEAVOX transforms satellite Earth observations into reproducible, musically expressive soundscapes without requiring backend servers or software installation.

Users explore a frozen UTC satellite observation through dual synchronized views—an equirectangular 2D analytical map and a WebGL 3D globe with a procedural aircraft and horizon camera—while sampling real-time visual intensities of liquid rain and solid snow. Powered by a deterministic Web Audio API engine (GEO-RAIN-001 v3), GEAVOX translates precipitation magnitude into granular impulse density, harmonic scales, and stereo spatialization, strictly distinguishing verified dry zones (0) from out-of-coverage regions (no-data). By combining scientific rigor, transparent artistic rules, and an optional cultural accompaniment layer, GEAVOX makes planetary Earth data accessible and engaging.
details:
What It Does & How It Works

GEAVOX is an interactive, browser-based geospatial sonification explorer designed for NASA’s "The Earth Information Jukebox" challenge. Users pilot a virtual aircraft across a frozen UTC global precipitation snapshot (2026-11-15T16:30:00Z) from NASA’s Earth Information Center (EIC) Content Database and Scientific Visualization Studio (SVS 4285, GPM/IMERG) to hear planetary precipitation patterns in real time.

Key Architecture & Features

- Triple-Mode Synchronized Views: Users switch seamlessly between a high-resolution 3600x1800 2D equirectangular (Plate Carrée) map, a synchronized Split 2D + 3D Globe view, and a full WebGL 3D Globe powered by Three.js featuring a procedural exploration aircraft, sweep footprint cone, and Google Earth-style horizon chase camera.

- Interactive Flight & Jukebox Navigation: Supports both Autopilot across 4 curated global satellite tracks and free Manual Pilot control using WASD/Arrow keys (with Shift turbo) or click-to-teleport/waypoint drawing anywhere on Earth.

- Two-Clock Separation & Scientific Integrity: GEAVOX separates the frozen satellite observation timestamp (timestamp_utc) from spatial playback time (playback_seconds). Sampling reads NASA’s official alpha precipitation layer (imergert_alpha.now.png) alongside official liquid rain (rainbarblack2.png) and solid snow (snowbarblack2.png) color scales, reporting normalized visual intensity (0.000–1.000) without inventing physical mm/h units, while strictly distinguishing verified dry zones (0) from out-of-coverage polar caps (|lat| > 87°) or < 50% valid coverage (no-data silence).

- Deterministic Sonification Engine (GEO-RAIN-001 v3): Built with pure Web Audio API and a seeded Mulberry32 PRNG (seed 20261115), the engine translates normalized liquid and solid precipitation intensities into granular impulse densities (0.6–24 Hz), phase-specific timbres, stereo panning by longitude, and selectable harmonic profiles, grounded in auditory texture statistics (McDermott & Simoncelli, 2011) and musical perception regularities (Savage et al., 2015; Mehr et al., 2019). Includes a live 60 FPS transect and oscilloscope visualizer, JSON contract inspector, accessible text table, bilingual ES/EN UI, automated validation tests (T01–T08), and an optional, toggleable Web Audio cultural accompaniment layer.

Tools, Languages & Hardware

Developed in Vanilla JavaScript (ES6 modules), HTML5 Canvas, CSS3, Three.js (WebGL), and Web Audio API on a MacBook M5, requiring zero backend servers or installation.

Impact & Creativity

GEAVOX bridges rigorous Earth observation and musical accessibility, enabling students, researchers, and visually impaired users to compare dry coastlines, convective storms, snowfall, and satellite coverage limits through reproducible sound.
